name: ai-memory
tagline: Give your coding agent a long-term memory - persistent, searchable context that survives across sessions.
sentence: ai-memory is an MCP server that stores project decisions, patterns and conventions so your coding agent remembers what it learned.
what_happened: **Three unpatched security advisories found Oct 9 2026.** GHSA-2jrq-p5rw-6wvv (low): wiki page reads and writes follow symlinks out of the project tree. GHSA-7qj3-7wqw-m5w6 (moderate): database user without write access can modify shared global preferences. GHSA-vh98-jf5c-jw45 (low): ignore_paths capture exclusion fails open for a path with a leading double slash.

**Previously pulled and restored.** ai-memory was pulled on Oct 2 2026 for earlier advisories, then restored after those were confirmed fixed in version 2.5.2. These are new advisories published Oct 9.
why_fail: **Three advisories with no patched version.** The latest published release is 2.6.2 and none of the three advisories list a fix.
**Symlink traversal lets files outside your project be read or written.** GHSA-2jrq-p5rw-6wvv means a wiki page operation could follow a symlink to read or modify files outside the project directory.
**Privilege escalation in shared setups.** GHSA-7qj3-7wqw-m5w6 means a user without write permission can still change global preferences.
if_used: Check for unexpected files or changes in your project directory, especially if you use symlinks.
If you share the database with others, audit the global preferences for unauthorized changes.
Watch for a patched release. Once these advisories have confirmed fixes, the gate will re-check automatically.
